A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CORAL research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and relocated or renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-generation results on CIFAR10-LT, CIFAR100-LT, and CelebA-5, plus appendix experiments on hyperparameters, balanced datasets, and memorization.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds ImageNet-LT results, T2H results on CelebA-5, and an ambient-space contrastive comparison.

M1.justification: The bottleneck projection head, supervised contrastive objective, time-dependent weighting, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. V2 explains why the projection head is unnecessary during sampling, but does not establish a changed inference procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds ImageNet-LT generation at 64 × 64 resolution, covering 1,000 categories and approximately 115,800 training images. This substantially broadens category coverage beyond CIFAR10/100 and CelebA-5. Existing balanced and limited-data CIFAR scenarios remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds T2H to the CelebA-5 comparison. New Table 4 evaluates an Ambient Space Contrastive comparator on CIFAR10-LT and ImageNet-LT; the text describes it as similar to DiffROP, rather than identifying it as a DiffROP reproduction. The established baseline suite otherwise remains.

E3.justification: V2 adds an ImageNet-LT protocol with 300,000 training steps for all models and evaluation of 50,000 generated samples against 20,000 balanced validation images. It also changes the CelebA-5 preprocessing description from cropped to resized images. Existing CIFAR budgets remain unchanged; newly disclosed evaluation details do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a focused comparison of ambient versus latent contrastive regularization. V1's per-class FID analysis at imbalance 0.01 and CelebA-5 qualitative baseline comparison are removed. Hyperparameter sweeps, balanced-data experiments, sample-size analyses, memorization examples, and latent visualizations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: New ImageNet-LT results report CORAL FID 16.11 versus DDPM 17.08, CBDM 22.66, and T2H 18.59. Table 4 adds ambient-space comparator FIDs of 5.85 on CIFAR10-LT and 24.73 on ImageNet-LT; CelebA-5 gains T2H FID 9.50. Existing Table 1 entries and balanced-CIFAR scores remain unchanged. Results displayed in v1 Figures 3 and 15 are removed.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the same mathematical content, and neither version supplies additional theoretical results or proofs. Corrections to set notation and the contrastive-temperature subscript are not substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The central entanglement diagnosis, CORAL contribution, and improved tail-generation claims remain. V2 removes Section 1.1's explicit priority claim that CORAL is the first diffusion method combining a bottleneck projection head and supervised contrastive learning without altering the generative decoder.

C2.justification: V2 explains the projection head as separating contrastive and generative objectives while preserving intraclass diversity, and interprets the new comparisons as evidence of better scaling to many classes. It adds possible text-to-image and LoRA applications. The computational-cost limitation remains, while the explanation connecting CORAL to reduced guidance requirements is removed.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link, balanced reference-data and uniform class-sampling disclosures, the 5,000-versus-5,000 per-class FID procedure, and ImageNet-LT setup details. It removes the CelebA-5 20% subset statement and sampling batch sizes of 4,096 and 2,048. These omissions do not establish that the underlying experiments changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for ImageNet-LT, projection-head benefits, latent diffusion, and LoRA, while retaining the existing related-work framework. It also removes the explicit first-method claim and expands the positioning of latent versus ambient contrastive regularization.

P1.justification: Changes are localized: expanded architectural explanations, a new Future Directions paragraph, conversion of loss-definition bullets to prose, and condensation of Appendix D. The main section and appendix organization remains, and the publication footer changes from an under-review preprint to NeurIPS 2025.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 2 and 4 and expands Table 1 with a baseline row, resolution labels, and revised highlighting. V1 Figure 8 moves into the main text as v2 Figure 3; the original imbalance-0.01 plot and Figure 15 are removed. Most other visual material is retained with relocation or renumbering.

improvement.justification: ImageNet-LT and the ambient-space comparison broaden empirical support for CORAL, while evaluation disclosures and a code link improve reproducibility information. The net gain is limited by incomplete specification of the new comparator and ImageNet hyperparameters, removal of useful diagnostics and the CelebA subset disclosure, and Appendix D's retained claim that T2H is unavailable for CelebA-5 despite its new reported scores.
